To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the interferometer images show that χ Cyg is a pulsating Mira star with a radius varying by 5.1% and an acceleration of the CO layer compatible with the gravitational field of a 2.0 solar mass star.

the interferometric observations of the S-type Miras show the existence of a molecular layer with an angular acceleration compatible with free-falling and that the derived mass is compatible with the fundamental pulsation period.

the interferometric diameter of χ Cygni is a function of time with a 5.0 mas amplitude, that the star is a 2.2 solar mass Mira, and that a warm molecular layer falls freely in its gravitational field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new technique to measure stellar masses and parallaxes of Mira stars.
the determination of fundamental parameters of Mira stars.
the study of the pulsation mechanism of Mira stars, which are fundamental for our knowledge of the late stages of stellar evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have obtained a precise measurement of the radius, mass and distance of χ Cygni.
the interferometric technique is the best method available to determine the radius of Mira stars, and that it is also the best method available for measuring the mass of Mira stars.
the Mira star χ Cyni is a fundamental pulsator, with a mass of ~2 solar masses, a radius of ~12 solar radii at maximum, and a parallax of ~0.17 mas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the star χ Cygni is a 5.8 solar mass Mira pulsating in its fundamental mode, with a radius of about 1.3 solar radii, and with an outer layer that is falling freely under the action of gravity.
we have shown that interferometry is a very powerful technique for the study of Mira variables.

we have shown that the pulsations of a Mira star can be mapped in detail by combining interferometric angular measurements with radial velocity data, allowing for the determination of its distance and mass.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interferometric imaging of pulsating stars can be used to derive their distance and mass.
interferometry can be used as a novel tool to determine the fundamental parameters of Mira stars.
a star can be observed as it pulsates, allowing the study of stellar pulsations in unprecedented detail.
